name: finish
summary: finish accepted

differential_diagnoses.name: Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome
differential_diagnoses.why: Considered due to the presence of an ossicle at the inferior patella seen on X-ray and edema on MRI. However, it is less likely because MRI demonstrates complete discontinuity of the tendon with high signal filling the gap, which represents a structural rupture rather than the apophysitis/inflammation characteristic of SLJ syndrome.

differential_diagnoses.name: Patellar tendinopathy with partial tear
differential_diagnoses.why: Considered as a spectrum of patellar tendon injury. However, it is less likely because the imaging evidence (MRI axial and sagittal views) shows complete disruption of the tendon fibers with a gap filled by fluid/high signal, rather than just intrasubstance degeneration or a partial defect.

key_findings.fact: X-ray frontal view shows normal alignment of the left knee with preserved joint spaces and no obvious fracture or dislocation.
X-ray lateral view shows a small ossicle located inferior to the patella at the patellar tendon insertion site.
MRI sagittal PD fat-sat shows high signal intensity (edema) at the inferior pole of the patella with disruption of the patellar tendon insertion and surrounding soft tissue edema.
MRI sagittal PD fat-sat contact sheet shows extensive high signal in the anterior knee region with disruption of the patellar tendon, consistent with a complete tear.
MRI axial PD fat-sat shows extensive anterior soft tissue edema with disruption of the patellar tendon, appearing discontinuous with high signal filling the gap.
MRI coronal PD fat-sat shows normal alignment of the knee joint with preserved joint spaces and no obvious meniscal tear or ligamentous injury.

uncertainty: The ossicle at the inferior patella on X-ray may represent a chronic change from prior Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome or an acute avulsion fragment associated with the tear, though the complete tendon discontinuity dominates the clinical picture.
